The bilinear term also assumes rank-1 structure---a single contamination dimension per model---while contamination may be domain-specific (e.g., coding vs.\ reasoning), requiring a higher-rank decomposition $\sum_r c_{nr} \cdot e_{ir}$ that the current model does not capture.

5	Post-hoc power analysis indicates $N \approx 17$ for 80\% power to detect $\Delta\tau = 0.071$; the $N = 8$ evaluation has ${\sim}$50\% power, explaining the non-significant bootstrap result. tool_args.old_string: We enforce non-negativity and sparsity of $c_n$ through a hierarchical HalfNormal prior. A global shrinkage scale $\sigma_c \sim \text{HalfNormal}(1.0)$ controls the overall contamination level, and per-model raw effects $c^{\mathrm{raw}}_n \sim \text{HalfNormal}(1.0)$ are scaled to obtain $c_n = c^{\mathrm{raw}}_n \cdot \sigma_c$. The HalfNormal support restricts $c_n \geq 0$, and the hierarchical structure provides adaptive shrinkage: when the data support low overall contamination, $\sigma_c$ contracts toward zero, pulling all $c_n$ values down. Models with genuine contamination retain large $c^{\mathrm{raw}}_n$ relative to the group. The remaining priors are $\theta_n \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 1)$, $b_i \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 1)$, $d_j \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 0.5)$, and standard uniform on thresholds $\tau_k$.
